title: Biscuits and gravy
subtitle: Southern buttermilk biscuits with sausage cream gravy
excerpt: Biscuits and gravy is a Southern American breakfast of fluffy buttermilk biscuits split and covered in a thick, creamy sausage gravy made from crumbled pork sausage, flour, and whole milk. The gravy is white and peppery. It is a substantial breakfast that goes together in about 30 minutes.
sourceNotes: Southern American culinary tradition. Biscuits and gravy is documented in Edna Lewis, The Taste of Country Cooking (1976), and in WPA Southern state food surveys. The combination of a quick bread (biscuit) with a milk-based sausage sauce has been a Southern breakfast staple since the late eighteenth century.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The biscuits can be made ahead and reheated. The gravy is best made fresh.

glossaryTerms.definition: A leavened quick bread made with flour, butter, and buttermilk, similar in texture to a British scone but less sweet. The term biscuit in the American South refers to this soft, fluffy bread, not a baked crisp biscuit.

content.text: Biscuits and gravy has two parts: fluffy

made in the same way as British scones (flour, cold fat, buttermilk, minimal handling), and a pork sausage gravy made in the same pan the sausage was cooked in. The fat in the pan is the base of the sauce. It comes together quickly once the biscuits are in the oven.

Heat the oven to 220°C. Combine {{plain-flour}} of flour, {{baking-powder}} of baking powder, bicarbonate, and {{salt-table}} of salt. Rub {{unsalted-butter}} of cold butter cubes into the flour until the mixture resembles coarse breadcrumbs. Make a well in the centre and pour in {{buttermilk}} of cold buttermilk. Stir with a fork until just combined.

Turn onto a lightly floured surface and pat out to 2.5 cm thickness. Do not roll. Cut into rounds with a floured cutter or the rim of a glass and place on a lined baking tray. Bake for 12 to 14 minutes until risen and golden.
Crumble {{sausage-meat}} of sausagemeat into the frying pan over medium-high heat. Cook for 6 to 8 minutes, breaking it up, until browned all over. Do not drain the fat.

Sprinkle the gravy flour over the sausage and stir to coat. Cook for 1 minute. Gradually pour in {{whole-milk}} of milk, stirring constantly to prevent lumps. Simmer for 5 minutes, stirring, until thick and creamy. Season with {{black-pepper}} of black pepper and salt. The gravy should be very peppery.
Split the warm biscuits and ladle the gravy generously over them. Serve immediately.

items.cause: Overworked dough, or old baking powder.
items.fix: Handle the dough as little as possible. Stir until just combined and pat out rather than rolling. Fresh baking powder is important.

items.cause: Milk added too quickly or flour not properly cooked into the fat.
items.fix: Add milk in a slow stream, stirring constantly. If lumpy, pass through a sieve while still hot.

items.cause: Too much flour or too little milk.
items.fix: Add more milk in splashes over low heat, stirring until the desired consistency is reached.

content.text: A pinch of cayenne in the gravy adds heat. Sage-flavoured sausagemeat gives a more herby gravy. A tablespoon of hot sauce stirred into the gravy at the end is the Southern kitchen refinement. Serve with fried or scrambled eggs alongside.

Biscuits and gravy is a core Southern American breakfast, tied above all to rural Appalachian and Deep South cooking. It is filling, cheap, and fast, which explains its place as a working breakfast. Soft bread and creamy peppery gravy is one of the most comforting breakfast combinations in the American repertoire.
